questions.question: Identify the term used for the removal of internal organs from a poultry carcass. / a). Trussing b). Giblet removal c). Evisceration d). Dressing
questions.solution_html:
• C Evisceration
  • Immediately after slaughter, meat may appear purplish-red due to deoxymyoglobin.
  • After slaughter, muscle glycogen is converted into lactic acid.
  • Fresh eggs have thick, firm albumen (egg white) with a high proportion of thick albumen.
  • Rapid and uniform heating of suitable food materials.
  • High initial investment and equipment cost.
  • Document verification: Check animal identification, ownership and relevant movement
  • or health records.
  • Beef: Meat obtained from cattle.
  • Red meat: Rich in myoglobin; examples include beef, mutton and chevon.
  • Meat is placed inside a suitable, low-permeability packaging material.
  • Selection and cleaning: Fresh eggs of good quality are selected and cleaned
  • appropriately.
  • Edible by-products
  •  Liver: Rich in iron, vitamins and protein.
  •  Heart: Used as food and contains high-quality protein.
  •  Kidneys: Used for human consumption after proper inspection.
  •  Tongue and brain: Consumed in some regions.
  •  Tripe: The edible stomach lining of cattle and other ruminants.
  •  Blood: Used in certain food products where permitted.
  • Raw material selection: Select fresh fish or suitable fish material.
  • Contains a high concentration of protein.
  • Used as a protein supplement in foods.
  • Effect of oxygen availability on meat colour
  •  Myoglobin is the principal pigment responsible for meat colour.
  •  In the absence of oxygen, deoxymyoglobin gives meat a purplish-red appearance.
  •  When the package is opened and meat is exposed to oxygen, oxymyoglobin forms and
  • produces a brighter red colour.
  •  During prolonged storage, metmyoglobin may accumulate and produce brown
  • discoloration.
  •  Therefore, purple meat in an unopened vacuum pack is not necessarily spoiled.
questions.final_answer:  Therefore, purple meat in an unopened vacuum pack is not necessarily spoiled

questions.question: Select the factor most likely responsible for excessive drip loss after thawing of a / frozen fish product: a). Repeated freezing and thawing b). Proper rapid freezing c). Good glazing d). Constant frozen storage
questions.solution_html:
• A Repeated freezing and thawing
  • During storage, oxymyoglobin is oxidized to metmyoglobin, which gives meat a brown
  • colour.
  • During ageing, enzymes break down proteins and other muscle components, producing
  • flavour precursors.
  • The albumen becomes thinner and more watery as its protein structure changes.
  • Better retention of colour, flavour, texture and nutrients in some foods.
  • Electrode corrosion and electrochemical reactions may occur.
  • Examination in motion: Observe walking, gait and signs of lameness.
  • Pork: Meat obtained from pigs.
  • Processed meat: Meat preserved by curing, smoking, fermentation or other processing;
  • examples include ham, bacon and sausages.
  • The package is sealed to prevent air from entering.
  • Separation: The egg contents may be separated into yolk, albumen or whole egg
  • according to the required product.
  • Bones
  •  Used to produce bone meal, gelatin and certain mineral products.
  •  May be processed into animal feed ingredients where legally permitted.
  • Size reduction: Mince the fish to increase processing efficiency.
  • Provides protein in a compact, low-moisture form.
  • Used in fortified foods and nutritional formulations.
  • Effect on lipid oxidation
  •  Oxygen promotes the oxidation of unsaturated fatty acids in meat.
  •  Lipid oxidation produces peroxides and secondary compounds that can cause rancid
  • odours and flavours.
  •  Vacuum packaging reduces oxygen exposure and generally slows lipid oxidation.
  •  Consequently, it can help preserve flavour and nutritional quality during storage.
  •  Oxidation is reduced, not completely prevented.
questions.final_answer:  Oxidation is reduced, not completely prevented
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Distinguish the contractile unit of a muscle fibre. / a). Sarcomere b). Myofibril c). Myosin d). Tendon
questions.solution_html:
• A Sarcomere
  • The rate of colour change depends on oxygen availability, pH, temperature and storage
  • conditions.
  • Cooking produces characteristic meat flavour through Maillard reactions and fat
  • oxidation.
  • The thick albumen height decreases, resulting in a lower Haugh unit value.
  • Reduced damage caused by prolonged heating.
  • It requires careful control of voltage, current and processing conditions.
  • Clinical examination: Check visible body condition, eyes, skin, mucous membranes and
  • abnormal discharges.
  • Mutton: Meat obtained from adult sheep.
  • Reduced oxygen slows the growth of many aerobic spoilage microorganisms.
  • Filtration: Shell fragments and other foreign materials are removed.
  • Fat and adipose tissue
  •  Rendered to obtain tallow or lard.
  •  Used in soap, candles, industrial products and certain food applications.
  • Extraction: Use an appropriate food-grade process, often involving solvents such as
  • ethanol or isopropanol, to remove fat and odorous substances.
  • May retain minerals and other nutrients, depending on processing.
  • Applied in bakery and cereal-based products.

questions.question: Interpret the purpose of evisceration during carcass processing. / a). Remove internal organs b). Improve meat tenderness c). Increase moisture content d). Add preservatives
questions.solution_html:
• A Remove internal organs
  • Microbial growth and prolonged storage can cause discoloration.
  • B. Changes in meat flavour
  • Spoilage microorganisms may produce unpleasant odours and flavours.
  • Therefore, higher Haugh unit values generally indicate better albumen quality and greater
  • freshness.
  • Haugh unit: An index used to evaluate egg interior quality based mainly on albumen height and
  • egg weight.
  • Suitable for foods containing particles suspended in liquids, such as soups and sauces.
  • Disadvantages
  • It is less suitable for foods with very low or highly variable electrical conductivity.
  • Identification of abnormalities: Look for fever, injuries, swelling, weakness or suspected
  • infectious disease.
  • Lamb: Meat obtained from young sheep.
  • It reduces oxidative rancidity, surface discoloration and moisture loss.
  • Pasteurization: Liquid egg is pasteurized using a validated time-temperature treatment to
  • reduce pathogenic microorganisms.
  • Intestines
  •  Processed into natural sausage casings.
  •  Some intestinal tissues are used in the production of pharmaceutical materials.
  • Separation: Separate the protein-rich material from the extraction liquid.
  • Can help improve the protein content of foods.
  • C. Applications
  • Used in selected animal feed formulations where appropriate.
  • D. Limitations
  •  May develop a fishy flavour or odour if processing is inadequate.
  •  Excessive heat may reduce protein functionality.
  •  Some people may experience allergic reactions to fish proteins.
  •  Production cost and solvent recovery requirements may be high.
  • Overall advantages of vacuum packaging
  •  Extends shelf life under suitable refrigeration.
  •  Reduces oxidative rancidity.
  •  Minimizes moisture loss and contamination after packaging.
  •  Preserves flavour and quality for a longer period.
  •  Facilitates storage and transportation.
questions.final_answer: Option (b) Changes in meat flavour
